transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Darren Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Allisyn, Head of Data), Ethan Cole (CTO), Ruth Bell (Security Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: Prospect evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for inference. Focus on SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs, data retention.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. got Darren our SE here. can i get quick intros?
[00:00:10] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here, head of data at Allisyn, and i own the analytics side.
[00:00:15] Ethan Cole: Ethan, CTO, i'll be involved on infra decisions.
[00:00:19] Ruth Bell: Ruth, security engineer, i'll own the compliance questions.
[00:00:23] Darren Ortiz: Hey folks, Darren, solutions engineer. we're here to understand your security gating and map Redwood to your controls.
[00:00:35] Maya Chen: quick agenda — cover compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), auth (SSO/SAML), access controls (RBAC), keys/encryption options, and logging/retention. then i'll cover high-level hosting options and we can flag items for follow up. sound good?
[00:00:48] Ethan Cole: yep sounds good. I want to land on whether we can use hosted or need dedicated/private for PCI-like workloads, and what gaps we'd need to fill.
[00:00:57] Ruth Bell: quick one — do you have SOC2 type II and ISO27001 in your binder? we will need artifacts for vendor risk review.
[00:01:05] Maya Chen: yes, we have SOC2 Type II, and an ISO summary. i'll send the attestation and scope. we also have our security whitepaper. link note in chat: redwood security pack (auto-note).
[00:01:15] Priya Nair: will that include network diagrams and where data at rest resides?
[00:01:20] Maya Chen: yes basic network diagrams plus data residency statements. for hosted, tokenization and logs are retained for billing and observability but customers can opt out of retention for certain tiers.
[00:01:32] Ruth Bell: when you say opt out — can we have zero retention of request/response payloads?
[00:01:37] Darren Ortiz: currently hosted has configurable retention controls; full no-retention of PII is possible with dedicated or private where you control the storage. hosted can be configured to drop payloads, but there are audit and billing traces that remain — like token counts, model used, timestamps — typically hashed.
[00:01:53] Ethan Cole: so to meet our compliance we may need dedicated or private. what is the typical traffic profile that would force us there?
[00:01:59] Darren Ortiz: latency and isolation drive it. if you have strict data residency + customer-managed KMS + absolute zero payload retention, private is the cleanest path. dedicated gives isolation and customer keys via KMS integration for many customers; hosted gives fastest onboarding.
[00:02:15] Priya Nair: your docs use 'Redwood Dedicated' and 'Redwood Privatee' in some places — can we get the precise differences in a one-pager?
[00:02:24] Maya Chen: totally, i'll attach a one-pager that maps features across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:02:30] Speaker 1: (mumbled) -- also curious about the canary / rollback story for model updates.
[00:02:35] Darren Ortiz: we support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallbacks. all rollout events are logged to audit streams that can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[00:02:45] Ruth Bell: about SSO — we run Okta. do you support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[00:02:51] Maya Chen: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for RBAC and org management. we integrate with major IdPs including Okta, Azure AD, and G-Suite.
[00:03:01] Ruth Bell: is SSO available on the control plane for private deployments as well?
[00:03:05] Darren Ortiz: yes, private deployments can point to your IdP — control plane supports SAML and you can host a private control plane if needed. for air-gapped we have different setup steps.
[00:03:15] Ethan Cole: what's the auth model for API calls? api keys? jwt?
[00:03:19] Maya Chen: primary auth is API tokens. for enterprise we support token rotation, short-lived tokens backed by SSO, and mTLS can be arranged for private/dedicated.
[00:03:30] Priya Nair: KMS question — can we bring our own key and have decryption only in our VPC?
[00:03:35] Darren Ortiz: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for dedicated and private. hosted supports KMS integration with cloud KMS for customer-managed keys where allowed by region, but there are caveats around key escrow — we'll send exact flow diagrams.
[00:03:48] Ruth Bell: we need key rotation policy and proof we never hold plaintext in logs. is that documented?
[00:03:55] Maya Chen: yes we have a KMS integration doc and encryption whitepaper. generally we encrypt at rest and in transit; keys are never stored in plaintext and audit logs do not contain PII. i'll share specifics.
[00:04:06] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) ok
[00:04:10] Priya Nair: audit logs — can they be exported to our SIEM and do you preserve request identifiers for tracing?
[00:04:16] Darren Ortiz: audit logs can stream to your SIEM via secure forwarding (syslog/HTTPS). we include request ids, model variant, timestamps, and error codes. payloads are not included unless explicitly enabled.
[00:04:29] Ruth Bell: retention windows — we need 7 years for some items. is that possible?
[00:04:33] Maya Chen: long-term retention can be arranged for audit logs in dedicated/private. hosted retention tiers exist up to 1-2 years by default; custom retention >2 years usually needs a dedicated plan.
[00:04:45] Ethan Cole: when you say billing traces remain, can we get a minimal set retained for regulatory proof without request content?
[00:04:50] Darren Ortiz: yes, minimal billing traces (token counts, model name, timestamp, tenant id) can be retained without payload content.
[00:04:58] Priya Nair: are there SOC2 carve-outs for your edge service that does continuous batching? sometimes runtime telemetry seems like it could leak info.
[00:05:06] Maya Chen: we can point to the sections in SOC2 about telemetry and sampling. runtime telemetry is aggregated for performance; any PII is hashed/removed per customer settings.
[00:05:15] Ruth Bell: do you have penetration test / third-party vuln scan reports?
[00:05:19] Maya Chen: yes we have pentest summaries and remediation notes. will attach in the package.
[00:05:25] Ethan Cole: network-wise, do you support customer-managed VPC peering or private link?
[00:05:30] Darren Ortiz: supported. for dedicated and private we do VPC peering/private link and restrict egress. hosted has regional endpoints and restricted egress IP ranges for allowlisting.
[00:05:40] Priya Nair: any time we do a PoC we need reproducible perf numbers. will you run a latency/throughput benchmark with our sample loads?
[00:05:46] Darren Ortiz: yes, we can run a benchmark. typically we do a small pilot on dedicated or hosted with a dedicated pool; i'll prepare a test plan.
[00:05:55] Ruth Bell: compliance paperwork — do you provide a completed vendor risk questionnaire or a SOC2 bridge letter if the last SOC2 was outside our window?
[00:06:02] Maya Chen: we provide SOC2 report, attestation, and a bridge letter when applicable. also we can fill standard VRQs (vendor risk questionnaires) — we have a template.
[00:06:12] Speaker 1: (unclear) pricing for dedicated — is it a commit?
[00:06:16] Maya Chen: yes dedicated is typically committed monthly/annual capacity. Darren can share typical sizing and cost levers (batching, quantization).
[00:06:25] Priya Nair: very important — isolation between tenants. we are multi-tenant internally and need hard RBAC scoping.
[00:06:31] Darren Ortiz: RBAC is role-based, and we can do namespace-level isolation and per-token scoping. for private you can get full tenant separation.
[00:06:39] Ruth Bell: auditability of RBAC changes — do changes generate audit events?
[00:06:43] Darren Ortiz: yes, changes to roles/permissions produce audit logs with actor, timestamp, and delta. these can be exported to your SIEM.
[00:06:52] Ethan Cole: curious about incident response — do you offer a shared playbook and SLA for incidents affecting model availability or security?
[00:06:59] Maya Chen: we have an incident response plan and offer SLAs on Dedicated. we'll share the IR playbook summary and escalation contacts.
[00:07:08] Priya Nair: for PII handling, we need a pattern for redaction in prompts. do you have guidance?
[00:07:13] Darren Ortiz: yes we have prompt redaction guidelines and automatic prefix-KV caching that avoids storing sensitive prefixes when configured. some of the terms in our docs are 'KV cache' but sometimes SRT transcribed as "K-V cash" in earlier notes, just ignore that.
[00:07:28] Ruth Bell: any regulatory restrictions on model training using customer data?
[00:07:32] Maya Chen: our terms prevent using customer payload for model training by default on enterprise agreements; we'll provide contractual language.
[00:07:40] Ethan Cole: what's the onboarding timeline to get something in prod for a small PoC?
[00:07:44] Darren Ortiz: for hosted it's a matter of days, dedicated usually 2-4 weeks to provision capacity and hook up KMS/SSO, private a few weeks more depending on networking.
[00:07:55] Priya Nair: can you send a sample network diagram for dedicated with KMS flow?
[00:07:58] Maya Chen: yes, i'll include.
[00:08:01] Speaker 3: (rustling)
[00:08:05] Maya Chen: quick recap: i'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, pentest summary, KMS & SSO integration docs, and a one-pager mapping hosted/dedicated/private features. Darren will prepare a PoC test plan and cost/latency spreadsheet. Ruth to send required audit fields and retention windows. agreed?
[00:08:25] Priya Nair: yes agree.
[00:08:27] Ethan Cole: agree.
[00:08:29] Ruth Bell: agree.
[00:08:31] Maya Chen: ok we'll follow up in email with attachments and link for the deep technical dive for the week of 1/18. thanks everyone.
[00:08:40] Darren Ortiz: thanks all.

End of transcript.

References in chat: Redwood security pack (SOC2/ISO), KMS integration diagram (to be attached), PoC test plan template (to be shared).

Notes on transcription quality: some names and product words mis-transcribed (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Privatee").
